_doc: The book registry. One entry per sourcebook this catalog cites, keyed by
the .cache/books/<slug> directory name.
`source_book` is free text in every table that holds it, and three separate
mechanisms parse it: resolveBookSlug (a row -> its cached pages),
drift-check's citation check, and the extraction prompt that fills the field
in the first place. Before this file each one guessed differently, and the
312 gear rows spelling the Palladium Fantasy main book `Palladium RPG Main
Book` resolved to nothing at all - every word of that title is generic, so
the word-overlap route is disabled by design and the initialism route needs
a `pf` the title never spells. An alias list is the only route they have.
title          the canonical spelling. The extraction prompt offers these
as the allowed values, so a NEW row should use one.
aliases        every OTHER spelling production actually contains, seeded
from the live vocabulary on 2026-08-27. A row cites its
book with a ` p.N-M` suffix; that is stripped before the
match, and matching ignores case and punctuation.
source_pdf     basename of the PDF the cache was built from, as the
manifests record it - or would be built from, for a book
with no cache yet. null when no copy is on hand.
source_pdf_dir the directory that PDF was read from. With source_pdf
it is the whole recovery record for a cache: .cache/
books/ is gitignored by design - it is the full text of
books Palladium still sells - so a cache is rebuildable
with one ocr-book.py run per book, and a PDF nobody
kept is not rebuildable at all. null when source_pdf
is. These PDFs are the only irreplaceable artifact in
this pipeline; this field says where they were.
printed_pages  the book's own last printed FOLIO, not the PDF page count.
With page_offset this GATES the citation check: a cache
holding fewer pages than the book has is not consulted,
whatever the PDF it was built from happened to hold. These
two outrank the manifest's own copies, because a manifest
derived from a truncated cache reports the truncation.
The two differ by the offset plus whatever unnumbered ads
the scan carries. null when it has never been measured.
page_offset    cache file page = printed folio + page_offset. Measured
with detectPageOffset over the cache. null when unknown.
page_offset_exceptions
ordered [{ printed_through, offset }] for a book that does
NOT paginate constantly. First match wins, everything past
the last falls through to page_offset. The entries below
are the list of which books carry one, and a cache
manifest.json cannot express this key at all. A majority
vote over a whole book cannot see a split: one minority
region is 11 pages against 287. class-check
--field-sources reports every region it detects, so the
next book with a split announces itself.
note           why a value is what it is, when it is not simply measured.
Entries under `books` are sorted by slug, and smoke fails if they are not.
Two book sessions in parallel each register a book; appended at the end,
their entries touch the same lines and conflict, while a sorted insert
usually lands them apart. No lookup depends on the order: registryBookSlug
walks every entry and refuses an ambiguous match. The extraction prompt
lists the titles in this order, which is presentation only.
Adding a book means adding an entry: class-check warns about a source_book
that matches no title and no alias, and does not fail on it. Nothing here is
required for a cache to exist, and a slug with no cache resolves to null.
Two gear provenance markers are NOT books. They say where a price came
from, not which book, and they are listed under `not_books` rather than
left out: left out, `Estimate - no published price found` resolved to `pf`
for 104 rows, because the initialism route reads e-n-p-p-f and finds `pf`
inside it. Anything in `not_books` resolves to nothing, by both routes.

triax.title: Rifts World Book 5: Triax and the NGR
triax.source_pdf: Rifts- World Book 5 Triax and the NGR.pdf
triax.note: Cached 2026-08-28 from a SCAN - no text layer, --probe medians 0 chars/page across all twenty samples. printed_pages corrected 222 -> 224 on 2026-09-07, in the batch that closed this book's classes: the last printed folio is 224, the Experience Tables, which carries its folio plainly. Printed 223 is an unnumbered Europe map and p225 is a back-cover advertisement. The survey asked for this in the book's FIRST data PR and four data PRs went by without it; nothing broke, because printed_pages only gates the citation check by requiring the cache to hold at least that many pages and the cache holds 225 - but a row cited to p.224 would have been citing a page the registry believed the book did not have. The THIRD zero-offset book here after potm and ww: printed N is cache pNNN, and read-columns.py N. Verified by folio rather than assumed - 177 pages agree at +0 against 1 at +1 - which matters because a zero offset leaves no discrepancy to explain when a page reads wrong. The five disagreements are OCR misreading the folio itself (p134 reads 693), not an offset region. This note said read-columns.py N+1 until 2026-08-30 and that was wrong, the same error the phase-world note carried: ocr-book.py writes cache pNNN from doc[pno - 1] and read-columns.py reads doc[n - 1], so cache pN IS read-columns.py N in every book, and page_offset relates that shared number to the printed folio and nothing else. It came from book-survey 0d's table, where 'zero-offset book' means printed N is pymupdf index N (potm, whose page_offset is 1) rather than page_offset 0 - two senses of the same phrase. Was a stub carrying one gear row and no copy on hand until the PDF arrived in the seven-book batch; the alias is live vocabulary that row resolves through and is kept.

underseas.title: Rifts World Book 7: Underseas
underseas.note: Cached 2026-08-28 from a SCAN - --probe medians 0 chars/page, OCR medians 5,668. THE SECOND BOOK HERE WITH A SPLIT OFFSET, after pf, and the first with a NEGATIVE one: printed 1-130 sit at +0 and printed 132-216 at -1, 101 pages against 74. A single number cannot describe it and a majority vote picks +0, which sends every lookup past 130 one page early. ocr-book.py measured -1 for the whole book, which is the same error from the other side. THE CAUSE IS A MISSING PAGE: printed 131 is absent from the PDF. File p130 carries folio 130 and ends mid weapons stat block; p131 carries folio 132 and opens mid-sentence. Printed 131 falls through to the -1 rule and lands on p130, which is printed 130 - wrong, but it is the nearest page that exists and nothing can cite a page the scan does not hold. printed_pages is 214, the last page of book content (the Experience Tables); printed 215-216 are numbered Palladium house ads. As of 2026-09-09 production held 87 gear rows, 74 spells, 50 vessels, 15 skills and 30 published classes citing this book.
